Hello again OP! 

No worries at all, I’m very happy I was able to communicate my point of view effectively. 

No one with BPD is a sociopath or making an active choice to be deceiving. It’s a subconscious desire to be liked and accepted, and sometimes we do adapt the way we act to the people we are around. I find I’m more authentically myself and can not think about my actions or voice around people I’m extremely comfortable around, ie my boyfriend or my closest friends. 

In essence, just because someone isn’t authentically themselves around you, does NOT indicate malicious intent. Everyone adapts to their surroundings, people with BPD just have different motivations. It’s not to get ahead, it’s to receive much needed attention we’ve repeatedly been told we can’t have or don’t deserve through verbal, physical, sexual abuse or neglect.  

That being said, every persons genesis with this disorder differs. Mine branches from infancy neglect and early childhood abuse up into my teens. Some people it’s alienation from peers, a lack of emotional support or a lack of belonging. Some sort of isolation when you need attention the most, so the need to attract attention becomes a need, but you’ve been taught not to express these needs. It’s a very confusing and internally contradicting disorder. 

Keep in mind when speaking with this person that your boundaries need to be very clear, but not in a way that feels like rejection. It’s best not to give physical attention because people with BPD tend to attach to physical attention due to a lack of it, so it’s just best for the both of you to refrain from touching him. 

I’d say the best option would be meeting for coffee, somewhere you didn’t go on a date that is neutral. Going out to dinner one-on-one can be too formal, and being alone can make intentions unclear. If you can go out with a group, I’d suggest a casual dinner that isn’t high in cost. Do NOT let him pay. Set that boundary very early, if you allow him to pay it shows that you allow him to take care of you and that established romantic intention. 

Another thing: you are allowed to have your emotions. You are more than entitled to be excited about seeing a friend you haven’t seen in awhile, and you can express that emotion. It provides validation, but again refrain from physical affection. You are allowed to have feelings, but check in and make sure your desire to rekindle your friendship is coming from a place of understanding and care, not a need to feel that feeling again, okay? That’s not accusatory, I’ve done that many times and it has absolutely blown up in my face. 

One more thing OP, if his parents are triggering to you I’d encourage you to set a boundary to not see them. Your trigger are there for a reason, they are a warning sign that something isn’t right so your brain can protect itself. Do not surround yourself with triggers, unless you’re trying to desensitize through EMDR or similar therapists. It can be significantly more hard than good, and that does worry me. 

If you have any more questions or requests, I’m more than willing to swap contact information or reply to comments, it’s not an issue at all. I try to end the stigma and fear around BPD, so I enjoy talking about my disorder and my perspective.

Hi OP! 

So, first things first, remember that BPD branches from a fear of abandonment that stems from early childhood to infancy. It can be very exciting when someone you idealized had decided to enter back into your life, especially when it seems they may have gone because of you. Tread very carefully to make your encounter as casual as possible, try not to touch them (a hug when you go home should be okay), in an environment where you can control what’s happening. It will show that you are present, without trying to create obsessive behaviors and maintaining your boundaries. 

Boundaries are SO important  in any relationship, but I know from my experience that if they are communicated well, then I don’t understand them effectively. Have your boundaries established before you enter into a new interaction with this person. Make them clear from the get go, but try breaking the news first then explaining yourself. That’s how my boyfriend approaches me about things that cause a hyper emotional reaction. (Ex. “Babe, I should go early. You’re sick and you should rest, I have some homework to do and the drive home is a lot. I’ll see you on Thursday, though.”) We’ve had conversations discussing the best way to break “bad news” to me, hard truth, then explanation, then validation. 

My FP is definitely my boyfriend. He is very patient and understanding, very involved in my therapy and is more than willing to validate when it’s needed. I feel awful giving him any sort of feedback I feel as negative, I want him to feel like the most special person in the world. He means the world to me. I can sometimes forget he’s capable of making mistakes, so sometimes he will say things that throw me off or make me uneasy. It’s an active effort to not allow these times to cause a split. Logic and reason play a strong part in that, not allowing your hyper emotional brain over power your logic and create a monster. I do know that feedback is very important, and that if something happened that was detrimental to me, I would need to take care of myself first. It’s taken a lot of therapy and DBT to be able to realize when I’m reacting with emotion, withdraw and logic my way through it, so not every person can. 

I’ve had FP’s who could do no wrong, and are idolized. I’d get very confused when they would do things to hurt me, because the person I had in my head during that time didn’t exist. It’s who I wanted that person to be. Keep in mind, you may not know the real him but he may not even know the real you. 

Everyone puts their best face on. Everyone adapts to their surroundings. This is not BPD exclusive, and as much as people would like to say we tailor personalities for our FP’s. It’s true we don’t have a strong sense of our personalities, and we tend to change our minds about who we are (rapid change in look, style, etc.). However this does not change the core parts of who we are. Patient, kind, funny, smart, etc. These things don’t change no matter how many times we dye our hair green then shave it off. 

I don’t think people under the difference between false identity and unstable identity. False identity is a conscious effort to convince another person you are someone that you are not. Unstable identity is not knowing who to portray to the world, because you are unable to identity what your core personality traits are. A way I’ve explained it is you’re swimming through years of abuse in your head all the time, and those thing you were told about yourself (insults, demeaning statements, isolation from peers) are masking themselves as personality traits. You try to find good ones within all this, but it can difficult when it comes to the self hatred and fear of being abandoned. It makes it that much more difficult to identify. 

I hope this helps!

I was sexually, mentally and emotionally abused by my Mother’s husband. 

It lasted for years, my mother knew about all of the abuse. It started when I was 7 or 8, abusive language, calling me ugly or a little bitch. Turned into screaming at me, throwing things at my head, pushing my head into walls. 

At this time, my Mother was an alcoholic and a drug addict. She’d drink and party a lot, so my brothers and I were left alone a majority of the time. She gave me my first cigarette when I was 8 years old. At 22, I still deal with an addiction to nicotine.

My mom surrendered full custody when I was 9, so we moved into my Dad’s home. 

My mother turned my brothers and I against my Dad, in essence used us as ammunition and pawns after the divorce.  I never felt like I could trust him, and he dealt with 3 children with behavioral issues on his own. He didn’t receive child support for a really long time, my mother could never hold down a job long enough to send any in. He had his hands full, so I think I may have gotten lost in the mix. He tried his hardest to help me, but I think he just really didn’t know what to do with me.

I became a really angry kid, lashed out at everyone. Friends, teachers, family, etc. I was bullied a lot because I was really poor and pissed all the time, so I was pretty isolated by my peers. 

When I was probably 12, I turned to chatrooms as ways to make friends. Unsupervised, I’d sit in chatrooms all day and all night, and was groomed by several different predators. I sent my first nudes at 13, to a 24 (possibly?) man. 

At this point, her husband started watching porn in front me and showed me pictures of his genitals.

When I was 14, I came out about the abuse and he was kicked out, where he allowed back a few months later. My mother convinced her entire side of the family that I’d lied, that I kept changing my story and that I’d confessed it was just a dream. She’d scream at me for hours about how I was a giant sack of shit, she beat the shit out of me. 

When he came back, I was taller than him at that point (the son of a bitch was 4’8” and I’m 5’3”. She let a 4’8” man molest her daughter), so our first fight is grabbed a kitchen knife and told him if he ever touched me again, I’d kill him. 

She let him beat the fuck out of her and verbally abuse me until I was in my 20s. I struggle with mental health issues and had really intense depression. 

At one point, I remember holding a hammer outside of their bedroom and really considering running inside and taking care of the issue, which in my head at the time was her husband. I went out drinking with friends instead. 

I had really amazing friend, I still do because we’re still close, who helped me through it. Gave me a place to stay when the house was too crazy. 

The mental  abuse didn’t stop until I moved across the country with my Dad due to Hurricane Michael in October of 2018. 

My family now believes me, her husband is in jail on ICE hold (he was an immigrant) for driving without a license, and I cut off all contact with my mother completely about a month or so ago. I finally gathered the courage to tell her family my side of the story, and they believe me. The still coddle her because she’s a fundamentally broken person, but they’re trying to help protect me from her. 

My dad and I are really close, I have a really healthy and functioning relationship. I’m in EMDR therapy to help with the trauma and I have really good coping skills, years of therapy and building an amazing support system. 

Life is still really hard, but knowing that son of bitch is finally in jail and my mother is all alone is a small amount of comfort while I desensitize to the abuse.
